research_notes: 2026-10-01 avenues: frozen/indexed APH occupations and maiden speech, contemporary legal press, Law Access 2017/18 and Law Society 2015/16 annual reports, public professional-history search. APH speech direct open failed; indexed official text available. Current personal biography URL inaccessible; primary-source search also returned unrelated results. No access controls bypassed.

Priority follow-up: CDPP appointment/cessation and ordinary versus ministerial DPC employment; precise iiNet and family-firm work/study overlaps. Obtain employment hours and unpaid/campaign leave, especially 2013 preselection and 2015/2016 campaigns. July 2013 full-time confirmation cannot support all 2011–16.

Check earlier Law Access reports for founding chair term and Street Law Centre/Starick governance leads. Public professional-history index supplied unverified month-level dates, not adopted without primary corroboration. Confirm other early work and career breaks; governance/service roles do not establish additional full-time employment.

Follow-up 2026-10-02: primary own biography, 2018 Hansard, indexed ARA 2003/2007 government records and December 2015 Pro Bono Centre report enrich excluded governance and volunteer history. Freehills commencement narrowed to March 2011 from public professional entry; direct profile 999.

Important identity caution: WA 2005/2006 Carpenter staff lists and 2017 MacTiernan acting-chief answer name Matthew Keogh. A separate government/resource-industry professional profile also exists. Neither ministerial lists nor Level 8/term-of-government status attributed to this MP without identity reconciliation; existing 2003–05 DPC role retained provisionally, no public years counted.

Law Access 2016/17 PDF timed out; indexed report identifies Adam Ebell as chair, so secondary aggregator claim Keogh chaired continuously December 2014–December 2017 is not accepted. 2017/18 director cessation remains supported. Street Law September 2013–July 2016 and CDPP October 2006–March 2011 aggregator ranges remain follow-up leads, not confirmed appointments.

Follow-up 2026-10-03: AIYD's published delegate biography establishes progression to Principal Federal Prosecutor and the corporate-crime subject matter, but not promotion month, hours or leave. Targeted CDPP, HSF, iiNet and public-profile searches did not supply primary appointment boundaries. WA parliamentary staff lists naming an older Matt Keogh include an ex-Builders Labourers Federation biography and therefore remain quarantined as a different person; they are not used to recategorise this MP's DPC spell. Next: original professional CV, employer records and Law Access/Street Law appointment reports.

Follow-up2026-10-04: Recovered Street Law Centre 2013/14, 2014/15 and 2015/16 primary reports. Added donated governance role from October2013, separate deputy-chair transition and resignation financial-year window. This supersedes unverified September2013–July2016 aggregator lead: neither of those month boundaries matches primary evidence. 2013 report link showed verification wall; used accessible public later reports without bypass. CDPP/iiNet/DPC ordinary appointment and private-practice dates, full-span hours and campaign breaks remain unresolved.

Follow-up2026-10-05: Recovered fullLawAccess2016/17report corroborates director-versusAdamEbellchair distinction. ExistingprimaryAIYDbiography supplies three omitted professionalgovernance roles: LawSocietyCouncil, YoungLawyersconvenor and AustralianYoungLawyerschair. Publicinterests transcription gives29July2016Councilresignation and15July2016StreetLawresignation; originalAPHdeclaration restrictedURL/HTTP403. StreetLawdate conflicts with2015/16annualreportperiod; retain nullendpointandbothclaims pendingprimaryreconciliation. Exact paidjob dates,hoursandcampaignleave still missing; cannot deriveFTtotals.
